text:
Insomnia 

 
 Keep your Mac awake. Give the session an end time. 
 

 
 A macOS menu bar app for timed awake sessions. Insomnia is an eye icon that
 lives in your MacBook menu bar. It has no Dock icon and no main window. Set
 how long your Mac stays awake, choose what happens when the lid closes, and
 see when something could not be undone.
 

 
 Website ·
 Install ·
 Using it ·
 Lid close ·
 Recovery ·
 Security 
 

 
 
 
 
 

 Use a stable, well-ventilated surface, not a closed bag. Insomnia is
 experimental. Recovery can fail, and a running timer is not a safety
 guarantee.
 Validation status · Apple's ventilation guidance

 
 
 

 Install

Requires macOS 26 or later on an Apple Silicon Mac.

For the newest nightly, write "the newest Insomnia nightly prerelease" in
place of "the latest stable Insomnia release". Nightlies are built from main 
on each day it has new commits. They have the newest code and may be broken.

To install a release yourself, follow docs/install.md. It
covers both channels, how to check the download, and v0.1.0 , which installs
differently. Settings General shows the installed version, and "Check for
updates" there tells you whether a newer release exists without installing
anything.

 Build from source

stable tag, or a nightly tag for the newest code:

 

 
 What the installer changes on your Mac 

The installer needs your password, because the sudoers rule is a system
file. It installs:

- The app, at /Applications/Insomnia.app .
- A recovery agent , a launchd job that runs every minute. If the app is
 gone when a session should have ended, the agent tries to undo the
 session's changes.
- A sudoers rule at /etc/sudoers.d/insomnia . A sudoers rule decides who
 can run what with sudo . This one lets your user account, not just
 Insomnia, run these four commands without a password:

 

Any program running as you can use that rule too, so review it before you
install. docs/install.md lists every
file and explains how upgrades replace them.

 

 Using it

1. Start. Click the eye in the menu bar, enter days, hours and minutes,
 and press Enter.
2. Add time. Click the eye or the countdown during a session.
3. End early. Press and hold the end control next to the countdown, or
 right-click the menu bar item and choose End session .
 To show only the eye, turn off "Show the countdown in the menu bar" in
 Settings. The eye opens while a session runs and closes when it ends,
 and the right-click menu also shows the time left.
4. Settings and status. Right-click the eye. Quit asks Insomnia to undo
 the session first, and it refuses while a change is still waiting to be
 undone. Saved audio for an output that isn't connected doesn't hold it up.
 Insomnia restores that output if it reconnects while the app runs, or at
 the next launch.
5. Menu bar style. The Menu bar picker in Settings General has four
 styles. Pills, the default, works as described above. Compact keeps only
 the eye in the bar, and a click opens the same pills, countdown and end
 ring in a small panel. Minimal is the eye with a ring for the time left:
 a click adds the default session length, and a 0.6 s hold ends the
 session. Popover shows the eye and, during a session, the time left to
 the minute (or the end time). Any click on it, left or right, opens a
 popover with time buttons, Custom fields for days, hours and minutes,
 the status, Settings and Quit. While a session runs it also has the
 ring you hold to end it. Popover style has no right-click menu, since
 the popover shows the same things.
6. One click. Turn on "Start a session with one click" in Settings 
 General, under the Menu bar picker. Then, in Pills, Compact and Popover,
 a click on the eye with no session running starts the default session
 length. Option-click opens the usual controls to pick another length,
 and in Popover a right-click or Control-click does too. A click during a
 session works as it does with the switch off, and never ends the
 session. If the start is refused, the pills, the panel or the popover
 opens with the reason. Minimal already adds the default length on every
 click, so Settings greys the switch out there. It is off by default.
7. Sounds. "Play a sound when you start or end a session" in Settings 
 General plays a short tone when you start or end a session from the
 menu bar. It is off by default, and while it is off Insomnia makes no
 sound and loads none. A session that ends without you asking (the
 timer, the recovery agent, Quit, a battery or heat rule, recovery after
 a crash) makes no sound. Nothing plays while the displays sleep or the
 lid is closed, and --session commands make no sound.

 nothing itself, so when the app isn't running it says so and exits 1.
 A build without this mode opens the menu bar app instead, so a script

install.title: Install
install.html:
Requires macOS 26 or later on an Apple Silicon Mac.

Paste this into your coding agent:

Install the latest stable Insomnia release by following https://github.com/krishhgg/Insomnia/blob/main/skills/install-insomnia/SKILL.md. If a step needs my password, give me the command to run in Terminal.

For the newest nightly, write "the newest Insomnia nightly prerelease" in place of "the latest stable Insomnia release". Nightlies are built from main on each day it has new commits. They have the newest code and may be broken.

To install a release yourself, follow docs/install.md. It covers both channels, how to check the download, and v0.1.0, which installs differently. Settings > General shows the installed version, and "Check for updates" there tells you whether a newer release exists without installing anything.

Build from source

Needs Xcode with Swift 6.2 or later. Replace v<version> with the latest stable tag, or a nightly tag for the newest code:

git clone --branch v<version> --depth 1 https://github.com/krishhgg/Insomnia.git
cd Insomnia
./scripts/install.sh
open "$HOME/Applications/Insomnia.app"
What the installer changes on your Mac

The installer needs your password, because the sudoers rule is a system file. It installs:

  • The app, at ~/Applications/Insomnia.app.
  • A recovery agent, a launchd job that runs every minute. If the app is gone when a session should have ended, the agent tries to undo the session's changes.
  • A sudoers rule at /etc/sudoers.d/insomnia. A sudoers rule decides who can run what with sudo. This one lets your user account, not just Insomnia, run these four commands without a password:
/usr/bin/pmset -a disablesleep 1
/usr/bin/pmset -a disablesleep 0
/usr/bin/pmset -b lowpowermode 1
/usr/bin/pmset -b lowpowermode 0

Any program running as you can use that rule too, so review it before you install. docs/install.md lists every file and explains how upgrades replace them.

usage.title: Using it
usage.html:
1. Start. Click the eye in the menu bar, enter days, hours and minutes, and press Enter.

  2. Add time. Click the eye or the countdown during a session.

  3. End early. Press and hold the end control next to the countdown, or right-click the menu bar item and choose End session. To show only the eye, turn off "Show the countdown in the menu bar" in Settings. The eye opens while a session runs and closes when it ends, and the right-click menu also shows the time left.

  4. Settings and status. Right-click the eye. Quit asks Insomnia to undo the session first, and it refuses while a change is still waiting to be undone. Saved audio for an output that isn't connected doesn't hold it up. Insomnia restores that output if it reconnects while the app runs, or at the next launch.

  5. Menu bar style. The Menu bar picker in Settings > General has four styles. Pills, the default, works as described above. Compact keeps only the eye in the bar, and a click opens the same pills, countdown and end ring in a small panel. Minimal is the eye with a ring for the time left: a click adds the default session length, and a 0.6 s hold ends the session. Popover shows the eye and, during a session, the time left to the minute (or the end time). Any click on it, left or right, opens a popover with time buttons, Custom fields for days, hours and minutes, the status, Settings and Quit. While a session runs it also has the ring you hold to end it. Popover style has no right-click menu, since the popover shows the same things.

  6. One click. Turn on "Start a session with one click" in Settings > General, under the Menu bar picker. Then, in Pills, Compact and Popover, a click on the eye with no session running starts the default session length. Option-click opens the usual controls to pick another length, and in Popover a right-click or Control-click does too. A click during a session works as it does with the switch off, and never ends the session. If the start is refused, the pills, the panel or the popover opens with the reason. Minimal already adds the default length on every click, so Settings greys the switch out there. It is off by default.

  7. Sounds. "Play a sound when you start or end a session" in Settings > General plays a short tone when you start or end a session from the menu bar. It is off by default, and while it is off Insomnia makes no sound and loads none. A session that ends without you asking (the timer, the recovery agent, Quit, a battery or heat rule, recovery after a crash) makes no sound. Nothing plays while the displays sleep or the lid is closed, and --session commands make no sound.

  8. From a script or an agent. The app's binary drives the running app:

    INSOMNIA=~/Applications/Insomnia.app/Contents/MacOS/Insomnia
"$INSOMNIA" --session start 7200    # two hours
"$INSOMNIA" --session extend 1800
"$INSOMNIA" --session status
"$INSOMNIA" --session end

    It starts, extends and ends the same session the menu bar counts down, with the same battery and heat rules, and prints one line. It changes nothing itself, so when the app isn't running it says so and exits 1. A build without this mode opens the menu bar app instead, so a script that may meet one checks InsomniaSessionCommandVersion in the bundle's Info.plist first.

You don't have to close the lid, and opening it doesn't end the session. When the timer or a battery or heat rule ends a session with the lid closed, Insomnia puts the Mac to sleep.

Insomnia stops system sleep, not display sleep, so the display still turns off when idle. If your Mac then asks for a password, agents that drive the screen stop at the lock screen. Keep the screen on and unlocked in Settings > General holds the display awake during a session, like caffeinate -d, so the screen saver never starts and the screen never locks while idle. With the lid closed, the display goes to brightness 0 instead of sleeping. Lock the screen under When the lid closes still locks the screen when you close the lid. When the session ends or Insomnia quits or crashes, macOS drops the hold, and the display sleeps and locks as before. Insomnia never changes the lock setting. The switch is off by default because anyone who opens the Mac during a session finds it unlocked, unless a lid close locked it.

On battery power, Insomnia turns on Low Power Mode below 40% and ends the session below 10%. Those are the defaults. You can change both in Settings, and an end floor of 0 turns the battery end off. The heat rules turn on Low Power Mode when the Mac gets seriously hot and end the session at critical heat. They are on by default, and Settings can turn them off. All of these rules only work while the app runs.

Before your first session, check Settings. Then run a short session you can watch, and read ~/Library/Logs/Insomnia/insomnia.log afterward.
